newsitem.title: UK: Cargill says works with IPE on gas oil delivery.
newsitem.headline: Cargill says works with IPE on gas oil delivery.

text.p: Trading house Cargill said on Monday it was working with the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on issues related to the November gas oil futures delivery.
A Cargill spokeswoman added by telephone the company had no comment on a statement by AIC that Cargill, the main long on the contract, had failed to take delivery of 160,000-190,000 tonnes.
"We don't have a specific response, at least at this point, on AIC's recent allegations," the spokeswoman said from Cargill's headquarters in Minneapolis in the United States.
"We are working with the IPE and expected that this will be settled through that channel," she added. She declined to elaborate.

She was replying to a request for comment on a statement by AIC, the main short, on Monday that Cargill had failed to lift between 160,000 and 190,000 tonnes of gas oil during the November 15-30 IPE delivery.

An AIC spokesman said earlier he planned to sell the product into the ARA barge market in order to mitigate what he called his company's damage arising out of the contract, adding the matter was now in the hands of the IPE.
The IPE said on Monday it was following procedures on the November contract. It declined to comment on the AIC statement.
